Phase 79 impl @ cc7eea5 (branch phase-79-watcher-stop-during-startup).
What changed (tagteam/watcher.py):
- _watch_sinked is now the catch: it calls _watch_started (the old body, renamed) and on KeyboardInterrupt logs the one 'Watcher stopped.' stop line and returns True. Loops keep their own handlers. Deviation from the plan's wording: the plan said 'catch around its whole body'; I split the function in two instead of indenting 50 lines, same boundary.
- write_pidfile moved inside the try/finally. Cleanup is _discard_own_pidfile: remove_pidfile(), and only if that removed nothing, unlink a pidfile that is a regular non-symlink file and does not parse. Called from this one finally, best-effort, as you asked; a readable record naming another pid is left alone.
- watch_command: one try around _install_sigterm_as_interrupt() and watch(); KeyboardInterrupt returns 0.
Tests (tests/test_watcher_lock.py, class TestStopDuringStartup, 9 cases):
- Subprocess, marker handshake via a test-only sitecustomize written to tmp: parked after the real write_pidfile (--poll; event trigger), parked after the real watcher_events.is_available (event trigger). Each asserts exit 0, no Traceback, no pidfile, lock free, one stop event last, no heartbeat. Waits bounded (marker 20 s, exit 15 s, shim park 30 s), child reaped in finally.
- In-process: interrupt inside the write leaving half a JSON document; interrupt after a whole write; readable pidfile naming another pid survives; pidfile=False leaves an unparseable watcher.json untouched; watch_command returns 0 when watch or the handler install raises.
Pre-fix evidence (same tests, unfixed watcher.py, scratch venv with .[event]): all three subprocess rows FAILED with 'AssertionError: exit -2', the CI symptom; in the project .venv the poll row failed the same way and the two event rows skipped.
Post-fix: test_watcher_lock + test_watcher + test_watchlog 147 passed, 2 skipped in the project .venv; in the .[event] scratch venv TestStopDuringStartup + TestSigterm 11 passed, five runs in a row.
Known limit: the project .venv has no watchdog, so the gate's run SKIPS the two event-trigger rows. They are proven only in the scratch venv and in CI on the PR.
Not covered: a KeyboardInterrupt in _watch_locked outside _watch_sinked (opening or closing the sink) is caught by watch_command (exit 0) but records no stop event; a second signal during cleanup (out of scope).
Full suite: the gate's run on this submission.

GATE: PASS | scope 2 paths | plan-doc ok | tests ok (2720 passed, 7 skipped, 6m39s)
checked: HEAD cc7eea5

Approved at cc7eea5. Reviewed watcher.py and the regression tests against the round-2 plan: the _watch_sinked/_watch_started split preserves the agreed catch boundary; pidfile creation is finally-protected; malformed-file cleanup is narrow, best-effort and called only under the watcher lock; readable records naming another pid survive; handler installation is inside the CLI catch. Marker-based subprocess tests exercise the shared write window and watchdog probe, and in-process tests cover interrupted whole/truncated writes and the pre-sink catch. Existing loop handlers are unchanged. No blocking findings. Verification: accepted GATE_PASS at HEAD cc7eea5 (2720 passed, 7 skipped), plus the submitted pre-fix failures and repeated scratch event-environment results; did not rerun the suite. The two event-trigger rows skip in the gate environment, so the planned PR CI check with .[event] remains required before merge. Opening/closing-sink stop-event and second-signal limitations are disclosed.
